reasons: Deviation classification is correct: original Section 20(d) imposes a blanket mutual consent requirement with no successor/affiliate carve-out and no reasonableness standard, so it fails the fallback (successor assignment on written notice; consent not unreasonably withheld) and Section 3(c) compounds it with a separate absolute bar on Customer assignment — squarely in walk-away territory per the rule.

Redline implements the rule's guidance: affiliate/M&A successor carve-out for Sparkling (Customer) on written notice, reasonableness standard for other assignments, no-competitor limit on Garman assignments, and a confirmatory statement that Customer change of control is not an assignment and gives Garman no termination/re-pricing right.
The p0033 conforming cross-reference ('except as permitted by Section 20(d)') is a minimal, necessary edit to prevent Section 3(c) from overriding the new carve-out; ratio 0.186.

Failed minimal-edit heuristic on p0142 (0.780) is acceptable here: the clause is a single short sentence and the required carve-out, consent standard and change-of-control language necessarily expand it; the original prohibition structure is preserved rather than replaced.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, and correctly reflects the playbook position without lecturing.
